# Results — Study 50 (High-Water): the 52-week-high effect on the S&P 500, 1996–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly returns of **398 current S&P 500
members** with ≥20y history (Yahoo) — a **survivor panel** (see the data stamp). Nearness = price ÷
trailing-12-month high; long the top quintile, short the bottom; the control is standard **12-2
momentum** (trailing 12 months, skipping the most recent — the Jegadeesh-Titman convention). As-of
2026-06; inputs fingerprint `c768f59e31fe`. (The panel cache is unchanged from the original run — the
fingerprint stands; the momentum control was re-run as 12-2 instead of a naive trailing-12, the cost
accounting fixed from round-trip to one-way, and the data-stamp span corrected.)*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "A distinct anomaly"? `BUSTED`

George & Hwang's claim has two parts — stocks near their 52-week high out-earn the rest, *and* this is
something different from momentum — and **neither survives here**, though for two differently-robust
reasons. The robust half: the nearness hedge is **0.82 correlated** with the standard 12-2 momentum
hedge — it is **not a distinct anomaly**, it's momentum measured a slightly different way, and a
correlation is insensitive to the panel's survivorship. The headline half needs its caveat said
plainly: the long-short shows **−8.4%/yr (Sharpe −0.40, Lo t −2.2)** on this panel, but the panel is
**current members filtered on ≥20y of history**, and that bias is not neutral to the *sign* — the
short leg holds names far below their high that we *know* survived into today's index, so their
rebounds are partly baked in (cf. [Study 33 Slingshot](../../33-slingshot/)). So the honest reading is
not "it reliably loses" but "**it lost on this survivor panel — the sign is partly manufactured by the
universe — and shows no premium anywhere**". No positive premium plus momentum-in-disguise is `NONE` /
`MIRAGE` / `BUSTED` either way.

## Data stamp

- **Universe**: 398 current S&P 500 members, ≥20y history, hedge sample 1996-01 → 2026-06, 366
  months (the 1995 panel start plus the 12-month nearness window), fingerprint `c768f59e31fe`.
- **Survivorship, named — and load-bearing here**: the panel conditions on the future twice
  (*current* membership × ≥20y-history filter). `high_water/data.py` raises a
  `SurvivorshipBiasError` unless the caller passes `allow_survivorship_bias=True`. For this study
  the bias does more than inflate magnitudes: the short side (fallen names) is guaranteed
  survivors, so the hedge's negative level is partly an artifact. The momentum *correlation* is the
  number this panel can support.

## The nearness long-short showed no premium — and it's just momentum

| | mean/yr | Sharpe | Lo t |
|---|---|---|---|
| 52-week-high nearness | −8.4% | −0.40 | −2.2 |
| 12-2 momentum (control) | +1.5% | +0.07 | +0.4 |
| **corr(nearness hedge, 12-2 momentum hedge)** | | **+0.82** | |

Two findings, with different evidentiary weight. First — the bias-robust one — the nearness signal is
**0.82 correlated** with standard 12-2 momentum: not a distinct anomaly, momentum with an anchoring
narrative. (Against the naive trailing-12-month momentum that includes the last month, the correlation
is 0.87; switching the control to the standard 12-2 convention barely moves it — the redundancy isn't
an artifact of how momentum is measured.) Second, buying near-high names and shorting far-from-high
names earned nothing positive anywhere on 1996–2026 large caps; the *significantly negative* level,
though, should not be stamped as a finding — it sits exactly where the survivor panel pushes it.

## No period delivered the promised premium

| | 52-week-high Sharpe |
|---|---|
| 1996–2012 | −0.52 |
| 2013–on | −0.18 |

Strongly negative early (the dot-com and GFC rebounds punished the short-the-fallen book — the
survivor effect at its sharpest), drifting toward zero since. No sub-period shows the positive premium
the strategy promises.

## …and costs only deepen the hole

The book replaces ~80% of a two-sided portfolio monthly ≈ **3.2× NAV of one-way trades** (an earlier
version of this page charged half that, treating the sweep as round-trip):

| cost (one-way) | net Sharpe |
|---|---|
| gross | −0.40 |
| 5 bp | −0.49 |
| 10 bp | −0.58 |
| 20 bp | −0.77 |

With nothing positive to start from, turnover is just a faster shovel.

## The honest takeaway

The 52-week-high effect is `BUSTED` where it can be tested robustly: it is **0.82 correlated with
standard 12-2 momentum** — not the distinct anomaly George & Hwang argued for, but momentum with an
anchoring story. And on tradable large caps it offered **no premium to harvest**: the measured
long-short was negative, a level our survivor panel partly manufactures (the short leg's rebounds are
conditioned in), but nowhere — in no sub-period, at no cost level — does a positive 52-week-high
premium appear. Whatever the original 1963–2001 sample showed, there is no separate 52-week-high
premium here. `NONE`, `MIRAGE`, distinct-anomaly claim `BUSTED`.
